fact: 1915年4月26日，英、法、俄与意大利在伦敦签订秘密条约，意大利放弃三国同盟义务，以取得特伦蒂诺、的里雅斯特、南蒂罗尔、戈里齐亚、伊斯特里亚与达尔马提亚北部为条件参战；条约要求意大利在一个月内对同盟国宣战。5月23日，意大利对奥匈宣战（对德国宣战迟至1916年8月28日）。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Italy and the Italian front, 1915–16
sources.quote: Great Britain, France, and Russia concluded on April 26, 1915, the secret Treaty of London with Italy, inducing the latter to discard the obligations of the Triple Alliance and to enter the war on the side of the Allies by the promise of territorial aggrandizement at Austria-Hungary's expense. Italy was offered not only the Italian-populated Trentino and Trieste but also South Tirol (to consolidate the Alpine frontier), Gorizia, Istria, and northern Dalmatia. On May 23, 1915, Italy accordingly declared war on Austria-Hungary. ... On August 28 Italy declared war on Germany.

sources.title: Military Wiki (Fandom), Italian Front (World War I)
sources.quote: the Treaty of London of 26 April 1915 in which Italy renounced her obligations to the Triple Alliance. On 23 May, Italy declared war on Austria-Hungary. ... The Treaty of London was concluded on April 26 binding Italy to fight within one month.

fact: 意大利军司令卡多尔纳把主攻方向定在威尼斯以东、伊松佐河下游谷地。1915年5月下旬开始的东进因伊松佐河涨水很快受阻，转入堑壕战。此后四次伊松佐河战役的日期为：6月23日—7月7日、7月18日—8月3日、10月18日—11月4日、11月10日—12月2日；大英百科称这四次「以28万人的代价换来的进展不值一提」。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Italy and the Italian front, 1915–16
sources.quote: The Italians' initial advance eastward, begun late in May 1915, was soon halted, largely because of the flooding of the Isonzo, and trench warfare set in. Cadorna, however, was determined to make progress and so embarked on a series of persistent renewals of the offensive, known as the Battles of the Isonzo. The first four of these (June 23–July 7; July 18–August 3; October 18–November 4; and November 10–December 2) achieved nothing worth the cost of 280,000 men

fact: 1915年8月21日，意大利对奥斯曼帝国宣战。此前意大利已于5月对奥匈宣战，但未对德国宣战。

sources.title: Alpha History, World War I timeline
sources.quote: August 21st: Italy declares war on Turkey.

fact: 1915年3月，即参战前两个月，意大利颁布法令规定全国只生产一种小麦面包，面粉出粉率由惯行的70%提高到80%，只分离麸皮；1916年3月出粉率进一步提高到85%，须把细麸掺回面粉。这项以「减少浪费」为名的强制配方，是意大利战时粮食管制的第一道命令。

sources.title: 1914-1918-online. International Encyclopedia of the First World War, Food and Nutrition (Italy)
sources.quote: in March 1915, two months before Italy's entry into the war, there was a decree establishing the first rule for the mandatory production of a single type of wheat bread. It would be made with flour no longer sifted 70 percent, as was customary, but 80 percent, with the separation, therefore, of only the bran from the selected flour. In March 1916, the sifting was increased to 85 percent

fact: 意大利的粮食问题在参战前已经爆发：由于海峡关闭失去俄国与罗马尼亚的惯常供应渠道，加上政府对进口小麦关税的处理失当，1914年12月即出现第一批小麦短缺与面包涨价。1915年5月参战后，农业劳动力被抽走（420万参战者中农民超过250万）、役畜被征用、化肥与农机进口几乎断绝，1915年收成很差，价格再度上涨，政府被迫放弃自由放任，开始实施价格上限与管制。

sources.title: 1914-1918-online. International Encyclopedia of the First World War, Food and Nutrition (Italy)
sources.quote: These conditions, combined with the refusal to purchase from America, considered too expensive, led, as early as December 1914, to the first wheat shortages and an increase in bread prices, with the risk of serious consequences for maintaining public order. Following Italy's entry into the war, in May 1915, the national production of wheat, together with all the other agricultural products, suffered significant deficits ... (the number of peasants at the front, out of a total of 4,200,000 men engaged in war operations, was higher than 2,500,000). ... The alarmed dispatches from local authorities, which reported the poor harvest of 1915 and new price increases, forced the government to abandon its out-and-out defence of liberalism

fact: 意大利在参战前后发行两次国债：1915年1月的第一次战争公债募得10亿里拉，1915年7月的第二次募得11.175亿里拉（含银行认购，不含殖民地与海外意大利人的认购）。经济学家伊诺第在1915年7月31日《经济学人》读者来信中指出，意大利国民收入约为5亿至6亿英镑，仅为英国的四分之一，因此这一数额在当时条件下应视为成功。

sources.title: Luigi Einaudi, The Italian war loan（《经济学人》1915年7月31日读者来信，Einaudi 基金会全文）
sources.quote: The results of the public loan issued in Italy by the Government towards defraying the war expenses have just been telegraphed. The amount is 1,117.5 million lire, including the subscriptions of the banks. ... That in a country like this the second war loan has reached the sum of 1,117 ½ million lire, after the first January war loan of 1,000 millions, is a proof of our economic growth ... our national annual income is valued at £ 2,000 to £ 2,200 millions; ours can be valued at only £ 500 to £ 600 millions

sources.title: Italy at War, 1915-1918（Warwick 大学经济系工作论文）
sources.quote: the clear backing of the Bank of Italy for easy credit and high bond prices, coupled with the continuing expectation of a short war, enabled the mushrooming public deficits of 1915/16 to be financed successfully by the Second and Third National Loans.

fact: 意大利银行以宽松再贴现与维持公债高价支持战时财政。1915年中至1916年中，高能货币名义值上升27.5%，同期批发价格上涨27.3%；1914年12月至1916年12月，商业银行存款实际增长约三分之一。战时财政主要靠发债而非征税或印钞。

sources.title: Italy at War, 1915-1918（Warwick 大学经济系工作论文）
sources.quote: In this period high-powered money did not increase in real terms. Its nominal value rose by 27.5 per cent from mid-1915 to mid-1916 with a 27.3 per cent increase in wholesale prices ... Commercial bank deposits rose by a third in real terms between December 1914 and December 1916

fact: 参战后意大利军方以预付货款方式为工业企业垫资：研究文献记载，军方采购部门（论文简称 AM）「慷慨的预付」使工业的资金需求得以由公共垫款满足，主持者为达洛利奥（Dallolio）。这一安排使企业在订货尚未交付前就拿到周转资金，是1915年意大利军火产能扩张的财政基础。

sources.title: Italy at War, 1915-1918（Warwick 大学经济系工作论文）
sources.quote: Bank deposits started to rise after the declaration of war, and the generous attitude of AM to procurement financing meant that industrial financial needs were being met by public advances granted by Dallolio's open-handedness.

fact: 1915年意大利420万参战者中农民超过250万，农业役畜被军队征用，化肥与农机进口几乎断绝；北方工业城市同时因军需订单吸纳大量劳动力。农村缺人缺畜、城市缺工，构成1915年意大利劳动力市场的两端紧缺。

sources.title: 1914-1918-online. International Encyclopedia of the First World War, Food and Nutrition (Italy)
sources.quote: the number of peasants at the front, out of a total of 4,200,000 men engaged in war operations, was higher than 2,500,000 ... The situation was further aggravated by the lack of work animals, which had also been requisitioned for the army, and by serious shortcomings, if not total absence, of imports of fertilizers and machinery.
